newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper rebounds by close on ASARCO news.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper rebounds by close on ASARCO news.

text.p: News that ASARCO has cut output at its Southern Peru Copper operations because of flooding woke a slumbering late session COMEX to shed its losses and close higher, traders said.
ASARCO said its 54.1 percent owned Southern Peru Copper plant curtailed both mine and smelter operations Monday afternoon after flooding damaged the company's railroad, roadways and tailings system.
"This seemed to give things a little bit of a boost," William O'Neill of Merrill Lynch said.
The company said there has been no significant damage to any of the major operations and ASARCO was assessing the effect on production.
Output at SPCC, one of the world's biggest producers, topped 307,581 tonnes of copper in 1996.
May COMEX settled 0.25 cent firmer at 113.00 cents a lb, traded 113.25 to 112.40 cents. Spot March went out 0.15 cent firmer at 115.70 cents.
Much of the session was lackluster and thinly traded following a smaller-than-expected dip of 1,775 tonnes in LME stocks Tuesday to 214,800 tonnes.

But O'Neill said the fillip provided by the ASARCO news was indicative of a copper market which was now well underpinned, with stocks down to just 2.7 weeks of supply and declining, and a healthy technical outlook.
"There is nervousness and this is a good seasonal period also. We should see the May contract head over 115.00 cents," O'Neill said.

Meanwhile, unusually warm winter weather in the Northeast and a new data collection method probably distorted robust new-home sales figures in January, economists said. Sales of new homes in January rose 8.6 to their highest in 11 years, but had been expected to dip after December's strong figure.
Construction is a key copper consuming sector.
